abstract: PesaCheck is an initiative of Code for Africa (CfA), which is the continent's largest open data/civic technology initiative with 103 full-time staff.
body_html:
PesaCheck is an initiative of Code for Africa (CfA), which is the continent's largest open data/civic technology initiative with 103 full-time staff (as at June 2022) in 21 African countries.

CfA is registered as a public benefit and tax-exempt non-profit organisation in South Africa (registration number: 168–092 NPO), as well as an NGO in Kenya (where it is registered as the Civic Media Foundation, with registration number CPR/2016/220101) and Nigeria (registered as the Civic Foundation Nigeria Ltd/Gte RC 1503312).

All CfA staff, including PesaCheck's team of 30 full-time editors/fact-checkers, are governed by the organisation's Charter, which explicitly states that CfA is non-partisan and non-aligned, and that CfA does not support or oppose any political party or candidate or cause.

CfA and PesaCheck's explicit mission is to instead support active and engaged citizenship, by promoting citizens' access to actionable evidence-based information that they can then use to shape public discourse, engage their leaders and hold their governments accountable.

Where PesaCheck has received funding, either directly or indirectly, related to a foreign government or one of its development agencies or sovereign funds, the terms of these grants include clauses that explicitly guarantee complete editorial control for PesaCheck.
headline: Non-Partisanship and Fairness
